---
title: "stringsAsFactors changed its default value in R 4.0"
ref: FCT-02
categories: [Factors]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'class(data.frame(x = "a")$x)'
reponse: '"character"'
attendu: "the same result whatever the R version"
versions: "Factors by default before R 4.0.0, text since"
source: "safer-r, R 4.0.0 NEWS, hadley/strict"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
customers <- data.frame(city = c("Lyon", "Paris", "Lyon"))
class(customers$city)
levels(customers$city)
as.numeric(customers$city)

options(stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
class(data.frame(city = "Lyon")$city)
```
:::

Every version offered in the menu is later than R 4.0.0: the block above shows the current behaviour. Before R 4.0.0, `customers$city` was a factor, `levels()` returned `"Lyon" "Paris"` and `as.numeric()` returned `1 2 1`.

## Why

Up to R 3.6, `data.frame()` and `read.table()` (hence `read.csv()`) turned text into factors by default. R 4.0.0 changed that default to `stringsAsFactors = FALSE`.

A script written before 4.0 that relies on `levels()`, `nlevels()` or on the factor codes keeps running, but now gets `NULL`, 0 or `NA`s. Only the numeric conversion leaves a warning. Adding `options(stringsAsFactors = TRUE)` at the top of the script does not bring the factors back: R accepts the option with a warning announcing its removal, and text stays text.

## The remedy

Write the argument explicitly, whatever value you want: the script then behaves the same way on every version.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
customers <- data.frame(
  city = c("Lyon", "Paris", "Lyon"),
  stringsAsFactors = TRUE
)
levels(customers$city)
as.numeric(customers$city)
```
:::
